title: The Lovers Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: The Lovers upright: choice, connection, values; reversed: feeling torn. Love, work, advice, Waite's 1911 text and the 1909 card. Draw it for your question.
image_alt: The Lovers, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a winged angel under a large yellow sun spreads its arms over a naked man and woman; a tree with a serpent stands behind her, a tree with flame-like fruit behind him.
capsule: The Lovers, card VI of the Major Arcana, stands for love, harmony and choice: a deep bond, or a decision that shows what you value. Reversed, disharmony takes over: values out of line or feeling torn. A warm card, it asks for honesty with yourself. On yes-or-no questions, upright means yes: two figures stand openly under the angel's blessing.

blocks.heading: What is on The Lovers card?
paragraphs: A huge winged figure fills the top half of the card, arms open above a man and a woman who stand apart on open ground. Waite: "The sun shines in the zenith, and beneath is a great winged figure with arms extended, pouring down influences" (p. 92).

The two people are "unveiled before each other, as if Adam and Eve when they first occupied the paradise of the earthly body" (p. 92). Behind the man Waite places "the Tree of Life, bearing twelve fruits"; behind the woman stands the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, and "the serpent is twining round it" (p. 92).

On the 1909 card the sun is a wide yellow disc with VI printed inside it; the angel has red wings and hair like flames, and a cloud lies between it and the couple. The fruits on the man's tree look like small flames, while the woman's tree carries round orange fruit, with a green serpent around its trunk. A single reddish mountain rises between the two. The woman looks up toward the angel; the man looks toward her.
Waite sums the picture up plainly: "This is in all simplicity the card of human love" (p. 92).

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about The Lovers?
paragraphs: The upright words are bright and simple: attraction, love, beauty, and hardships left behind. The reversed side is about plans that do not hold, and a second account adds obstacles of every kind; "contrarieties" is an old word for things that go against you.

Waite had little patience for earlier readings of this card. He wrote that "The old meanings fall to pieces of necessity with the old pictures", and that some of them were "false in symbolism" (p. 95).

blocks.heading: What does The Lovers mean upright?
paragraphs: Love in its fullest sense sits at the center of The Lovers upright: romantic love, a connection that is honest and unguarded, a partnership where attraction and shared values line up. With it often comes a choice that shows what you value most: a bond asks something of you, or a decision asks you to stay true to yourself.
Harmony here does not mean the absence of choices. It is the feeling of your heart and your values pointing the same way, so that a decision sits right on the inside and not only on paper.

Waite's list gives attraction and beauty, and the picture shows two people with nothing hidden from each other. If this is close to what you are living, ask: what would you choose if you were not afraid of missing out?

blocks.heading: What does The Lovers mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, The Lovers means disharmony: values that no longer line up, distance or conflict inside a bond, a connection that has lost its balance. Often it shows feeling torn, between what you want and what you think is right, or between two paths that both pull at you, and then it is an inner conflict more than a quarrel with anyone else. It can also show avoiding a choice, or an imbalance in which you give much more than feels good.
Waite's reversed words, failure and foolish designs, are about plans that fall through. The inner split is a modern reading, not Waite's.
Start by getting honest with yourself. A decision that matches what you care about tends to feel lighter once it is made.

blocks.heading: What does The Lovers mean in love?
paragraphs: No card is more tied to romance. Upright in a love reading, it means a strong romantic bond: attraction, closeness and a union where hearts and principles agree. When there is no partner, the card may mark an attraction that matters, or the work of getting clear about what you truly want before choosing anyone.

Already committed, you may hear it speak about honesty and deeper commitment: choosing the bond again, openly, as your own decision. It describes what you bring and does not predict where the relationship goes.

Upside down, it can mean a relationship out of balance: disconnection, arguments rooted in different values, or a commitment that feels uneven. For your part, notice where you feel pulled two ways, or where your choices drift from what you say you want. What would an honest next step look like for you?

blocks.heading: What does The Lovers mean for work and money?
paragraphs: A decision about direction that rests on what matters to you can be the work theme here: a role, a partnership, a project that fits who you are. It also favors good collaboration, where people pull the same way.

Money under The Lovers is about choices guided by values: spending and saving that match what you care about, and often a shared decision, such as a joint budget or a business partnership. Reversed, it points to money tension between partners, or to choices made only to please others or left to chance.

blocks.heading: What is The Lovers' advice?
paragraphs: Write down the choice in front of you and the value each option protects. Let the decision come from what you care about most, not from fear or habit, and make it openly, so that you can stand behind it later.

blocks.heading: Is The Lovers a yes or no card?
The Lovers as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: Few cards answer a feelings question as directly as The Lovers. Upright, its traditional meaning is love itself: strong attraction, deep affection and the wish to be together, the sense of a true match in heart and values, and a wish for the bond to grow into commitment. Reversed, the same feelings are read as mixed or out of balance: attraction held back by doubt, love that does not feel equal, or a heart pulled between two loyalties. As a person, the card can be a partner or a close ally, anyone with whom you share a real bond; it can also be you, standing at a crossroads.

pairs.text: Love meets commitment and shared tradition. Ask what promise you want to make.
A decision you keep putting off. Say both options out loud before you weigh them.
Connection next to attachment. Notice which bond feels free and which has become a habit.
A bond that grows into a sense of home. Notice what makes you feel you belong.

blocks.heading: The Lovers or the Two of Cups?
paragraphs: The Two of Cups also shows a couple. There "A youth and maiden are pledging one another", and a winged staff with a lion's head rises above their cups (p. 222). Today it is read as a meeting of equals built on respect. The Lovers is wider: a bond and a choice under a blessing from above, with your values at stake. A question about a relationship between two people leans toward the Two; a question about what you value leans toward The Lovers.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about The Lovers
paragraphs: What do I truly want here, beyond what looks good or safe?
Which of my values is at stake in this choice?
Where am I fully honest in this bond, and where am I holding back?

faq.q: Is The Lovers a good or bad card?
faq.a: Positive, for the most part. It brings closeness, attraction and the relief of a choice that fits what you care about. What it can expose is a split: wanting one thing and doing another. Even that harder side is useful, because it shows exactly where honesty is needed.

faq.q: Is The Lovers a soulmate card?
faq.a: It is often called one, because love and deep connection are its core meaning; still, no card can name a soulmate or promise that a bond lasts. Waite reads it as a card about human love (p. 92). What it can show is your side of a connection: whether what you feel matches what you believe in, and whether you choose openly.

faq.q: Does The Lovers always mean romance?
faq.a: No. Love sits at the center, but the card often turns up around a decision that tests your values: a job, a friendship, a direction in life. Older versions were even a family scene: Waite describes an eighteenth-century card "shewing father and mother, with their child placed between them" (pp. 14–15).

faq.q: Is The Lovers about choosing between two people?
faq.a: Rarely in such a literal way. Some later versions did show a man standing "between vice and virtue", but Waite says his card replaces them, going back to "first principles" (p. 92). On Arcana Diary the choice usually lies inside you, between a wish and a principle, or between two paths of your own.

faq.q: Does The Lovers mean he or she loves me?
faq.a: It is one of the strongest love meanings in the deck, not a verdict on one person. Upright, The Lovers is traditionally read as love returned: mutual attraction, warmth and the hope of commitment. Reversed, that reading turns to uncertain or uneven emotions. What a particular person feels only they can tell you, and the way they act over time says more than any single card.

waite.quote: Attraction, love, beauty, trials overcome. Reversed: Failure, foolish designs. Another account speaks of marriage frustrated and contrarieties of all kinds.
